cs.AI / 1 / 2611.23480
Diagnostic Accuracy and Navigation Behavior of Vision-Language Model Agents Reading Emergency CT and MRI Examinations
视觉语言模型智能体阅读急诊CT和MRI检查的诊断准确性与导航行为
Jonathan Lichtle, Aymen Meddeb, Antonin Birot, Ibrahima Niang, Lisa Gastaud, Riyad Hanafi, Sofiane Dujardin, Corentin Selomme, Guillaume Cachard, Aghiles Hamroun, Grégory Kuchcinski, Su Hwan Kim, Bastien Le Guellec
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Purpose. To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and image navigation behavior of vision-language model (VLM) agents under varying exploration strategies. Materials and Methods. In this retrospective study, six VLMs read 100 emergency CT and MRI examinations published in a public archive (March 2025-August 2026) under four conditions (free navigation, navigation from a key slice, and all slices or key slices in a single request), twice each (4800 runs). Nine radiologists read 30 of those cases. A large language model judge validated against two radiologists graded the answers. Conditions were compared with generalized estimating equations clustered by case. Results. Pooled accuracy was lowest under free navigation (32.6%; 391/1200), followed by navigation from a key slice (37.9%; 455/1200; P = .003), and highest with all slices (42.2%; 506/1200) or key slices (42.5%; 510/1200) in one request (both P < .001). On the 30 cases read by radiologists, freely navigating models were correct in 30.0% of runs (108/360) versus 77.0% for radiologists (208/270; P < .001). Models formed a first hypothesis after a median of 10.8% of the slices and kept it in 63.1% of runs (755/1196); final answers were correct in 12.4% of runs after a wrong first hypothesis (110/885) versus 90.4% after a right one (281/311; P < .001). Median stated confidence in the final answers was 90%, whereas 38.9% of them were correct (1861/4778). Conclusion. Across all exploration strategies, VLM agents remained far less accurate than radiologists. They adopted an early hypothesis and usually kept it, seldom correcting a wrong one.
Chinese Translation
目的。评估视觉语言模型（VLM）智能体在不同探索策略下的诊断准确性和图像导航行为。材料与方法。在这项回顾性研究中，六种VLM阅读了公共档案库中发布的100例急诊CT和MRI检查（2025年3月至2026年8月），并在四种条件下进行阅读（自由导航、从关键层面开始导航，以及在单次请求中提供所有层面或关键层面），每种条件各重复两次（共4800次运行）。九名放射科医师阅读了其中30例病例。由一名经两名放射科医师验证的大语言模型评判者给答案评分。采用按病例聚类的广义估计方程比较各条件。结果。合并准确率在自由导航下最低（32.6%；391/1200），其次是从关键层面开始导航（37.9%；455/1200；P = .003），而在单次请求中提供所有层面（42.2%；506/1200）或关键层面（42.5%；510/1200）时最高（两者P < .001）。在放射科医师阅读的30例病例中，自由导航模型在30.0%的运行中正确（108/360），而放射科医师为77.0%（208/270；P < .001）。模型在阅读了中位数10.8%的层面后形成首个假设，并在63.1%的运行中坚持该假设（755/1196）；在首个假设错误后，最终答案在12.4%的运行中正确（110/885），而在首个假设正确后则为90.4%（281/311；P < .001）。对最终答案所述置信度的中位数为90%，而其中38.9%是正确的（1861/4778）。结论。在所有探索策略下，VLM智能体的准确性仍远低于放射科医师。它们会形成早期假设并通常坚持该假设，很少纠正错误假设。

cs.AI / 2 / 2611.23483
SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
SpecLook：推测应看向何处，以实现快速且可靠的智能体式多模态大语言模型
Xi Ding, Jiawei Zhang
cs.AI · cs.CL · cs.CV · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. Our key insight is to speculate the agent's next observation, which, unlike a drafted answer, can be verified, corrected, and used to test the answer. We propose SpecLook, a training-free speculate-and-verify framework with three levels. A small model drafts a glimpse and re-answers from it, and the question ends if the answer is unchanged and confident. Otherwise, the agent's large model verifies and corrects the glimpse without tools, and their answers are fused. Only questions that still lack evidence reach the agent, in one forward pass that SpecLook-Fast skips, so no question runs the loop. The trace scores every answer's reliability without labels. Extensive experiments on V*, HR-Bench, and POPE show that both are more accurate than every baseline on every split. SpecLook reaches 87.2% and 86.2% mean accuracy with 7.7x and 4.7x speedups over the DeepEyes-7B and Thyme-RL agents, and SpecLook-Fast reaches 9.9x and 6.3x.
Chinese Translation
以图像进行思考的智能体式多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）将推理与放大工具调用交织在一起。然而，这种顺序循环很慢，且其答案不携带可靠性分数。此前对 token、推理步骤或答案的推测仍保留该循环，并且答案推测还会接受置信度高的错误。我们发现，该循环大多只增加一个放大步骤，而借助该步骤，小模型在大多数数据划分上领先于该智能体。我们的关键洞见是推测智能体的下一个观察；与草拟答案不同，该观察可以被验证、纠正，并用于检验答案。我们提出 SpecLook，一个无需训练的、具有三个层级的推测-验证框架。一个小模型草拟一个局部瞥见，并据此重新作答；如果答案保持不变且置信，则问题结束。否则，智能体的大模型在无工具条件下验证并纠正该局部瞥见，并将二者的答案融合。只有仍然缺乏证据的问题才会到达智能体，且仅通过一次前向传播，而 SpecLook-Fast 会跳过这次前向传播，因此没有任何问题会运行该循环。该轨迹无需标签即可为每个答案的可靠性评分。在 V*、HR-Bench 和 POPE 上的大量实验表明，两者在每个数据划分上都比所有基线更准确。SpecLook 在 DeepEyes-7B 和 Thyme-RL 智能体上分别达到 87.2% 和 86.2% 的平均准确率，并分别实现 7.7 倍和 4.7 倍加速；SpecLook-Fast 则分别实现 9.9 倍和 6.3 倍加速。

cs.AI / 3 / 2611.23702
KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
KnowMe Paper Radar：自动研究时代下有前景论文的轻量级发现
Zhuo Chen, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu, Lijun Wu
cs.AI · cs.IR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The growing volume of topically similar papers makes it difficult to identify new work that can offer useful research insights or methodological guidance. We present KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight discovery tool that combines multiple sources of evidence into personalized reading priorities. Users specify topics, priorities, exclusions and dates; the system brings together topical relevance, recency, author research histories, collaboration paths and direction-specific institutional context. By exposing each score component and its supporting sources, KnowMe helps readers select promising papers for their current questions and discover relevant work beyond familiar authors. Automatic acquisition, version merging and graph-cache reuse keep this workflow convenient without large language model (LLM) inference during ordinary use. Experiments on 174,640 acquired records show more than threefold faster repeated context preparation, while cached abstracts improve normalized discounted cumulative gain at rank 10 (NDCG@10) from 0.412 to 0.598 on expert-judged retrieval tasks. Complementary analyses examine how the same accumulated records support semantic retrieval, research-history modeling and literature-grounded planning. A browser interface and a structured command-line interface (CLI) make these capabilities available to both researchers and research agents, positioning KnowMe as a practical upstream tool for literature-informed recursive self-improvement (RSI) workflows.
Chinese Translation
主题相似的论文数量不断增长，使得识别能够提供有用研究洞见或方法学指导的新工作变得困难。我们提出 KnowMe Paper Radar，这是一种轻量级发现工具，它将多种证据来源组合为个性化的阅读优先级。用户指定主题、优先级、排除项和日期；系统汇集主题相关性、时效性、作者研究历史、合作路径以及方向特定的机构背景。通过公开每个评分组成部分及其支持来源，KnowMe 帮助读者为其当前问题选择有前景的论文，并发现熟悉作者之外的相关工作。自动获取、版本合并和图缓存复用使该工作流保持便捷，而无需在常规使用期间进行大语言模型（LLM）推理。在 174,640 条已获取记录上的实验显示，重复上下文准备速度提升超过三倍，而在专家评判的检索任务上，缓存摘要将排名第 10 的归一化折损累计增益（NDCG@10）从 0.412 提高到 0.598。补充分析考察了相同的累积记录如何支持语义检索、研究历史建模和基于文献的规划。浏览器界面和结构化命令行界面（CLI）使这些能力可供研究人员和研究智能体使用，从而将 KnowMe 定位为面向文献驱动的递归自我改进（RSI）工作流的实用上游工具。

cs.AI / 4 / 2611.23864
Asking but Missing: Decision Coverage in Natural-Language Data Querying
发问却遗漏：自然语言数据查询中的决策覆盖
Hangle Hu, Chenyu Hou, Bin Cao, Jing Fan, Wei Luo
cs.AI · cs.SE
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models are increasingly used to translate natural language questions about structured data into executable programs. A fundamental challenge is recognizing when a question admits multiple computational interpretations and identifying the decisions needed to resolve them. We investigate whether language models recognize these unresolved decisions before generating code, or silently adopt assumptions that may lead to incorrect results. We refer to the latter behavior as Underspecified Decision Completion (UDC). To distinguish different causes of UDC, we introduce Grounded Code Generation (GCG), a diagnostic protocol that separates the identification of unresolved decisions, their resolution using evidence, and their translation into executable code. By examining each stage separately, we can determine where the decisions responsible for incorrect results were first missed or mishandled. We evaluate this framework on BIRD-Pandas with twelve models. The results show that answering clarification questions consistently improves execution accuracy, yet substantial errors remain. Our findings suggest that the main difficulty lies not in answering clarification questions, but in recognizing which questions need to be asked in the first place.
Chinese Translation
大型语言模型越来越多地被用于将关于结构化数据的自然语言问题转换为可执行程序。一个根本性挑战是识别一个问题何时允许多种计算解释，并确定解决这些解释所需的决策。我们研究语言模型在生成代码之前是否会识别这些未解决的决策，还是会默默采用可能导致错误结果的假设。我们将后一种行为称为欠指定决策补全（Underspecified Decision Completion, UDC）。为了区分 UDC 的不同原因，我们引入有据代码生成（Grounded Code Generation, GCG），一种诊断协议，它将未解决决策的识别、利用证据对这些决策的解决以及将它们转换为可执行代码分离开来。通过分别考察每个阶段，我们能够确定导致错误结果的那些决策最初是在何处被遗漏或处理不当的。我们在 BIRD-Pandas 上使用十二个模型评估该框架。结果表明，回答澄清问题能够持续提高执行准确率，但仍然存在大量错误。我们的发现表明，主要困难不在于回答澄清问题，而在于首先识别出哪些问题需要被提出。

cs.AI / 5 / 2611.23908
Training-Free Domain Generation for One-Shot Federated Learning with Server-Side Pre-trained Diffusion Models
基于服务器端预训练扩散模型的单轮联邦学习免训练域生成
Yixuan Tong, Yuanguo Bi, Mingjian Zhi, Wenchao Xu, Yuan Wu
cs.AI · cs.CV · cs.DC
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
One-shot federated learning (OSFL) has attracted increasing attention for its ability to substantially reduce communication overhead by limiting client-server interaction to a single communication round. Nevertheless, this limited interaction makes learning from heterogeneous client distributions challenging. Diffusion-based OSFL approaches seek to address this challenge by synthesizing data that approximate client distributions. However, existing diffusion-based approaches often impose substantial computational costs on clients and lack effective visual guidance to generate data aligned with client distributions. To address these limitations, we propose FedDoG, a training-free Domain Generation framework that leverages server-side pre-trained diffusion models to synthesize data aligned with client domains. FedDoG extracts compact domain representations using a frozen image encoder, substantially reducing client-side computational and communication costs. These representations are incorporated into the diffusion model through a pre-trained image-conditioning adapter, thereby providing explicit visual guidance for domain generation. To further improve the quality of synthetic data, FedDoG adapts the strength of visual conditioning according to domain concentration and filters generated samples based on class consistency and predictive entropy. Experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that FedDoG generates higher-quality synthetic images and outperforms existing OSFL baselines in classification accuracy. Meanwhile, FedDoG reduces client upload and computation time by 99.9% and 91.5%, respectively. The code is available at https://github.com/YXTong17/FedDoG.
Chinese Translation
单轮联邦学习（OSFL）因其能够通过将客户端-服务器交互限制为单个通信轮次来大幅降低通信开销而受到越来越多的关注。然而，这种有限的交互使得从异构客户端分布中学习具有挑战性。基于扩散的OSFL方法试图通过合成近似客户端分布的数据来应对这一挑战。然而，现有的基于扩散的方法通常给客户端带来大量计算开销，并且缺乏有效的视觉引导来生成与客户端分布对齐的数据。为解决这些局限性，我们提出FedDoG，一种免训练的域生成框架，利用服务器端预训练扩散模型合成与客户端域对齐的数据。FedDoG使用冻结的图像编码器提取紧凑的域表示，从而大幅降低客户端计算和通信成本。这些表示通过预训练的图像条件适配器被纳入扩散模型，从而为域生成提供明确的视觉引导。为进一步提高合成数据的质量，FedDoG根据域集中度调整视觉条件作用的强度，并基于类别一致性和预测熵过滤生成的样本。在三个基准上的实验表明，FedDoG生成更高质量的合成图像，并在分类准确率上优于现有OSFL基线。同时，FedDoG将客户端上传时间和计算时间分别减少99.9%和91.5%。代码可在https://github.com/YXTong17/FedDoG获取。

cs.AI / 6 / 2611.24221
Learning to Coordinate: LLM-Guided Workflow Evolution for Token-Efficient Red Teaming
学习协调：面向令牌高效红队测试的 LLM 引导工作流演化
Xiaoyang Xing, Wenyu Dai, Xiaoliang Gong, Asoke K Nandi, Anthony Cohn
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Automated red teaming is essential for identifying safety failures in large language models (LLMs), but its practical scalability depends on the resources required to discover those failures. Multi-agent systems can combine complementary capabilities, yet repeated planning, redundant exchanges, and ineffective information routing can make their coordination expensive. Moreover, a target model's response indicates the outcome of a test without identifying which collaboration decision should change. We present Learning to Coordinate (L2C), an LLM-guided framework that evolves an executable multi-agent workflow for each red-teaming case. L2C represents agent responsibilities, execution dependencies, and input bindings in a versioned graph, and associates each graph with records of the information actually delivered and produced. A controller trained through supervised fine-tuning integrates these records with target responses, evaluator verdicts, and remaining budget to retain the workflow, refine instructions, restructure collaboration, or lock further editing. This design connects feedback to explicit changes in subsequent execution while allowing a useful organization to continue without repeated controller intervention. The evaluation protocol covers HarmBench with three execution backbones and two target models, together with component ablations, dataset transfer, and evaluator checks. Across the six executor-target configurations, L2C improves ASR over EvoSynth by 1.4 to 4.5 percentage points while reducing mean online tokens by 35.6% to 37.3%. L2C connects adaptive collaboration to the resource requirements of automated security evaluation.
Chinese Translation
自动化红队测试对于识别大语言模型（LLM）中的安全性失效至关重要，但其实际可扩展性取决于发现这些失效所需的资源。多智能体系统可以结合互补能力，但重复规划、冗余交互和低效的信息路由可能使其协调成本高昂。此外，目标模型的响应表明了一次测试的结果，却没有指出应改变哪一项协作决策。我们提出 Learning to Coordinate（L2C），这是一个 LLM 引导的框架，可为每个红队测试案例演化出一个可执行的多智能体工作流。L2C 在带版本的图中表示智能体职责、执行依赖和输入绑定，并将每个图与实际交付和产生的信息记录相关联。一个通过监督微调训练的控制器将这些记录与目标响应、评估器裁决和剩余预算整合起来，以保留工作流、细化指令、重构协作或锁定进一步编辑。该设计将反馈与后续执行中的显式变更联系起来，同时允许有用的组织方式在无需控制器反复干预的情况下继续运行。评估协议涵盖 HarmBench，使用三个执行骨干和两个目标模型，并结合组件消融、数据集迁移和评估器检查。在六种执行器-目标配置中，L2C 相比 EvoSynth 将 ASR 提高了 1.4 到 4.5 个百分点，同时将平均在线 token 数降低了 35.6% 到 37.3%。L2C 将自适应协作与自动化安全评估的资源需求联系起来。

cs.AI / 7 / 2611.24324
Reducing Inference Cost of Coding Agents with Timeout Cascades
利用超时级联降低编码智能体的推理成本
Boxi Zhou, German Sviridov, Dmitrii Ustiugov, Haris Javaid
cs.AI · cs.SE
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
AI coding agents have become one of the most popular applications of large language models. Yet, agentic AI comes at the cost of a tremendous amount of GPU compute resources, which limits its profitability and its viability at scale. In this paper, we investigate whether smaller, cheaper models can cut this cost without sacrificing accuracy. We evaluate 36 popular large and small open-weight models released since 2024 on a software engineering benchmark, and find that recent small models are closing the accuracy gap compared to their large counterparts. We investigate the structure of this gap and find that the gap is highly concentrated around hard tasks that small language models fail to solve while achieving remarkably good accuracy for easy and medium complexity tasks. Following this observation, we show that by utilizing a hybrid inference strategy that tries a small model first and escalates to a large one only when needed, we can achieve up to 33% reduction in total GPU-hour costs and 16.4% on all tasks from SWE-bench Verified, without sacrificing accuracy. Strikingly, this simple cascade nearly matches an oracle-style task router, highlighting a practical path for deploying cost-aware coding agents in production without complex learned task routers and with minimal engineering complexity.
Chinese Translation
AI 编码智能体已成为大语言模型最受欢迎的应用之一。然而，智能体式 AI 需要消耗大量 GPU 计算资源，这限制了其盈利能力以及大规模部署的可行性。本文研究更小、更便宜的模型是否能在不牺牲准确率的情况下降低这一成本。我们在一个软件工程基准上评估了自 2024 年以来发布的 36 个流行的大、小开放权重模型，并发现近期的小模型正在缩小与同类大模型之间的准确率差距。我们研究了这一差距的结构，发现该差距高度集中在小型语言模型无法解决的困难任务上，而在简单和中等复杂度任务上，小型语言模型能达到相当好的准确率。基于这一观察，我们表明，通过采用一种混合推理策略——先尝试小模型，仅在需要时升级到大模型——我们可以在不牺牲准确率的情况下，将总 GPU 小时成本最多降低 33%，并在 SWE-bench Verified 的全部任务上降低 16.4%。引人注目的是，这种简单的级联几乎可以匹敌 oracle 式任务路由器，突显了一条在生产环境中部署成本感知编码智能体的实用路径：无需复杂的学习型任务路由器，且工程复杂度极低。

cs.AI / 8 / 2611.24619
GateWatch: Low-Overhead LLM Monitoring with Boolean Circuits
GateWatch：基于布尔电路的低开销LLM监控
Firas Spanioli, Yaniv David
cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
As large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed, monitoring their behavior becomes important for detecting unsafe or unintended actions. Activation probes offer an efficient approach, but existing methods face trade-offs between accuracy, interpretability, and computational overhead. Probes on raw activations lack interpretable inputs, whereas sparse autoencoder (SAE) probes use interpretable features but often rely on additive classifiers and large SAE encoders, limiting interpretability and increasing memory overhead. We introduce GateWatch, a compact, interpretable classifier that expresses its entire decision rule as an explicit Boolean logic over a small number of binarized SAE features. We explore three approaches to constructing these circuits under a specified gate budget. For efficient deployment, GateWatchServe computes only selected SAE features, enables streaming of their binary values across layers during inference, and evaluates multiple GateWatch classifiers in parallel using compact lookup tables. Across 24 tasks on Gemma-2-9B, GateWatch achieves 80.49% mean test accuracy using only 3.8 SAE features and 3.5 logic gates per probe on average, just 1.17 percentage points below full 16K-feature SAE probes, while matching or outperforming them on 10 tasks and reducing probe memory by 99.98%. Inside vLLM, 1,000 concurrent multi-layer, multi-token GateWatch classifiers retain 97-98% of baseline throughput and 99.8% of KV-cache capacity.

Abstract
Small language models (SLMs) can run on commodity hardware and support privacy-preserving, on-premises clinical deployment, but their medical explanations are often short and poorly structured compared with large language models. Recent supervised approaches such as Meerkat transfer chain-of-thought reasoning into 7B-8B backbones, yet their training objective does not directly target the style or organization of the generated rationales. Building on the instruction-tuned Mistral-7B backbone, we investigate whether a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) step can improve explanation structure without human preference labels.We apply Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LoRA adaptation to 2,000 Meerkat-derived medical prompts, guided by a simple self-supervised reward that favors longer, lexically diverse, and well-punctuated responses while penalizing very short ones. Training for about 170 PPO steps on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU yields a stable increase in the average reward. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons show that the RL-tuned model produces longer, more organized, multi-point explanations while preserving the underlying medical content.We discuss the promise and the limitations of self-rewarded RL for shaping the style of medical explanations.

Siyuan Du, Yuxin Liu, Meng Tang, Haoran Li, Yechao Bai, Feiyang Pan, Jia He
cs.AI
large language model

Abstract
Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult. We approach these challenges through a policy-induced capability region, the set of states from which the current policy can reliably complete a task. Near its boundary, an agent may need only a few actions to reach a more solvable state, even when the goal remains distant. This reduces long-horizon learning to two coupled subproblems of reaching that state and completing the task from there. We address them with paired advantages and a progressive reverse-to-forward curriculum. The advantages provide separate signals for reaching more solvable states and completing the task from them, while the curriculum expands the capability region backward along successful reference trajectories and then into off-reference states through on-policy exploration. On ALFWorld and WebShop, our method outperforms competitive agentic RL methods at both model scales, achieving success rates of 90.1%/96.1% and 80.2%/82.6% with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, respectively.

Hardware Acceleration of Vision-Language-Action Models with Weight Precision Rising over the Flow Steps
权重精度随流步骤上升的视觉-语言-动作模型的硬件加速
Robin Geens, Simon Haepers, Jonas Crols, Chao Fang, Marian Verhelst
cs.AR
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Vision-language-action (VLA) models such as GR00T control robots through an action head: a diffusion transformer that turns noise into a chunk of actions in a few flow-matching steps. Every step re-reads all of the head's weights from DRAM but applies each weight to only about fifty tokens. Inference is therefore memory-bound, and its latency and energy are largely determined by the total number of transferred weight bits. We show that later flow steps attenuate the quantization errors of earlier steps, so the weight precision of an action head should rise over the steps. With plain per-channel rounding and without calibration or training, widths rising over the steps from 2 to 4 bits preserve the closed-loop success of robot policies. These widths transfer 25% fewer bits than 4-bit weights at every step. However, we show that on Jetson AGX Thor, current GPU kernels cannot exploit this per-step precision due to fixed overheads. We therefore present a programmable accelerator whose latency and energy both scale with the transferred weight bits. It decodes entropy-coded weights for bit-serial sub-arrays at the DRAM rate. Because the width changes per step, a run-time allocator divides these sub-arrays between the linear layers and the attention to balance their workloads. The same sub-arrays are thus capable of running action heads of different families and sizes, as well as a vision-language model. On the DRAM side, a requantizer and an entropy encoder at each bank let one stored 8-bit copy replace the copies of all widths. Simulated with LPDDR5X timing, our RTL implementation runs the GR00T N1.6 action head in 8.02 ms per inference with 2, 3, 3 and 4 bits in its four flow steps. With a copy per width and 50% of Thor's memory bandwidth, the accelerator runs this schedule 1.7x faster than Thor in NVFP4, at 9.1x less energy and equal closed-loop success.

Reliability by Architecture: Agentic Workflows for Validated Multi-Physics Simulation from Natural Language

Søren Taverniers, Eric Darve, Hamdi A. Tchelepi
cs.CE · cs.AI · physics.comp-ph
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Preparing, executing, and validating strongly coupled multi-physics simulations require expert time. Agentic workflows use large language models (LLMs) to coordinate them from natural-language descriptions, but reliability requires checks of physical consistency and fidelity to the problem description. Our agentic harness implements explicit task allocation: LLMs interpret user requests and simulator diagnostics, generate input components not covered by predefined construction rules, and propose repairs, while deterministic routines construct supported components and check inputs, edits, and results. We evaluate CO2-storage problems using the multi-physics simulator GEOS, from compositional flow to flow-poromechanics with frictional fault contact. In 80 attempts on two flow problems, grounding raises the proportion of structurally valid inputs from 5/20 to 20/20, but acceptance reaches 20/20 only with complete rule-based input preparation. With identical inputs, local repairs correct three seeded defects while preserving valid inputs. Supporting tests identify simulations passing physics checks despite differing from the problem description or reference results.

Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
追踪LLM推理轨迹中用于迭代博弈的表征
Chaipat Tirapongprasert, Rajarshi Das, Parijat Dube
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.GT
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. Ultimately, as multi-agent systems are more prevalent, our work opens the door to a more focused diagnosis of their strategic reasoning errors. For illustrative purposes, we offer an interactive visualizer of our methodology on selected sample traces at https://interp-self.github.io/gametrace/

Formal Adequacy Index (based on Polish-language material)

Paweł Patreucha
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Linguistic formality is one of the dimensions of stylistic variation in speech; however, simply measuring its level does not allow us to determine whether the chosen mode of communication is appropriate in a given situation. The aim of this article is to present the concept of a formal adequacy index (based on Polish-language material), which enables a quantitative assessment of how well the formality of a text matches the expectations arising from the communicative context. The proposed approach is based on the separate modelling of observed formality, determined on the basis of the linguistic features of the text, and expected formality, determined on the basis of the characteristics of the communicative situation. Adequacy is assessed by comparing these two measures, taking into account contextual tolerance thresholds, which may differ for a lack of formality and an excess of formality. The potential applications of the index are illustrated by an analysis of Polish-language emails containing apologies for being late, written by human language users or generated by a large language model. The implementation presented here is preliminary in nature and requires further calibration and empirical validation. The main contribution of this article is the proposal of a general methodological framework for the quantitative study of formal adequacy in various communicative contexts.

Dreaming Up Authors: Factual Prevalence and LLM Hallucinations in Academic Authorship Attribution
臆想作者：学术作者归属中的事实流行度与LLM幻觉
Sijia Zhong, Tamir Yirga, Yijia Ma, Thai Le, Yifan Hu
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely used for question answering but are prone to hallucinations, yet the underlying causes, particularly the role of factual prevalence in training data, remain underexplored. In this work, we study this through academic authorship attribution, hypothesizing that hallucinations are more likely for less prevalent papers. Using citation count as a proxy for factual prevalence, we curate a dataset of 1.92 million papers across eight scientific disciplines with stratified samples by citation level. Experiments on three state-of-the-art LLMs confirm our hypothesis, revealing a robust inverse relationship between hallucination rate and citation count across all models and disciplines, with hallucination rates exceeding 98% for rarely cited papers and falling below 37% for highly cited ones. Our in-depth analysis further shows that these failures primarily reflect retrieval limitations rather than knowledge absence, and hidden-state probing of open-source models shows that factual prevalence is encoded in pre-generation representations, providing convergent mechanistic evidence for the prevalence-hallucination relationship. The code and data are available at https://github.com/quinnzhong1/dreaming-up-authors.

Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated through their ability to predict future outcomes, implicitly assuming that predictive success reflects an understanding of the underlying system. However, accurate predictions can often be achieved without recovering the latent mechanisms that generate observable outcomes. To examine this assumption, we introduce LUCID, a benchmark that evaluates whether models can infer latent market structures from event descriptions and historical financial observations. Models generate event-induced causal graphs representing inferred market structure and are evaluated through a reconstruction-based framework. Our evaluation of 6 open-weight and proprietary LLMs shows that adding their generated graphs generally reduces reconstruction quality compared with using historical observations alone, although a few metrics improve. These findings suggest that inferring informative, event-specific market structures from observable evidence remains challenging for the evaluated LLMs.

Abstract
Researchers are increasingly using large language models (LLMs) to validate research questions. We find that LLMs make open research questions sound partly studied and overstate what related papers establish. Models recognize most of these overstatements when asked to check the papers' full texts separately. On 40 questions drawn from newly accepted papers, GPT-6-Astra correctly judges 98% to be unstudied, but states that status plainly in only 8% of ordinary answers. All six frontier systems show reporting gaps of 30-90 percentage points. Across 22 models given identical papers, higher capability is associated with more accurate judgments and larger reporting gaps. This reporting failure is asymmetric: models correctly identify studied questions in 88-100% of ordinary answers when we supply the answering papers. To correct this, we build a fixed answer from each model's judgment and separate checks of cited papers. This raises Astra's clear reporting of open status from 8% to 95%, with improvements in all six systems. Finally, we predict reviewers' novelty grades by combining several models' written ratings with a rule learned from graded examples, reaching the performance range reported by Think-Probe-Respond. Unlike TPR, our approach needs no access to model weights or internal activations, so it also works with closed-weight frontier models.

Beyond Replacement: Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models

Shuaidi Wang, Zhuocheng Gong, Xuejie Liu, Jianguo Li, Yu Zhang
cs.CL · cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer a flexible alternative to autoregressive models, enabling any-order infilling. While most existing decoding methods treat decoded tokens as fixed, some recent models allow previously decoded tokens to be revised only by replacing them with alternative tokens, a paradigm we refer to as replacement-only editing (ROE). Although ROE can correct individual tokens, it is inefficient for sequence shifts caused by missing or extra tokens and struggles when errors occur across many positions. To address these limitations, we propose LED (Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models), a post-training framework that extends ROE with insertion and deletion, enabling Levenshtein-style refinement of generated sequences. It uses two training designs. First, it reconstructs edit supervision on the fly during supervised fine-tuning using longest-common-subsequence alignment, enabling insertion and deletion learning without manually annotated labels. Second, it adopts multi-stage training, where the state from one stage becomes the input to the next, exposing the model to its earlier errors and enabling it to correct them. When applied to the 16B-parameter LLaDA2.1-Mini Base, LED raises the average score across twelve benchmarks from 54.86 to 57.10 under confidence-guided decoding while increasing tokens per forward from 6.14 to 7.05, whereas under confidence-free decoding it raises the average score from 27.52 to 47.19. We further show that LED achieves higher pass@k at large k than thresholded decoding without editing, demonstrating improved generation diversity and revealing the diversity potential of DLMs without confidence guidance. LED also improves robustness to large block sizes, raising the average score from 36.97 to 51.34 at block size 128. Together, these results suggest that LED supports more robust self-correction in DLMs.

扩散语言模型（DLMs）为自回归模型提供了一种灵活的替代方案，能够实现任意顺序的填充。尽管大多数现有解码方法将已解码的 token 视为固定不变，但一些近期模型允许仅通过用替代 token 替换先前已解码的 token 来对其进行修正，我们将这一范式称为仅替换编辑（replacement-only editing, ROE）。尽管 ROE 能够修正单个 token，但对于由缺失或多余 token 引起的序列偏移而言效率低下，并且在许多位置同时出现错误时也难以应对。为解决这些局限，我们提出 LED（Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models），这是一个通过插入和删除操作扩展 ROE 的后训练框架，能够对生成序列进行 Levenshtein 风格的细化。它采用两种训练设计。第一，它在监督微调期间利用最长公共子序列对齐即时重建编辑监督信号，从而无需人工标注标签即可学习插入和删除。第二，它采用多阶段训练，其中一个阶段的状态成为下一阶段的输入，使模型接触到其早先的错误并能够纠正这些错误。当应用于 16B 参数的 LLaDA2.1-Mini Base 时，LED 在置信度引导解码下将十二个基准的平均分数从 54.86 提高到 57.10，同时将每次前向的 token 数从 6.14 提高到 7.05；而在无置信度解码下，它将平均分数从 27.52 提高到 47.19。我们进一步表明，在较大的 k 值下，LED 相比未编辑的阈值化解码取得了更高的 pass@k，这表明生成多样性得到改善，并揭示了 DLMs 在无置信度引导下的多样性潜力。LED 还提高了对大块尺寸的鲁棒性，在块尺寸为 128 时将平均分数从 36.97 提高到 51.34。总体而言，这些结果表明 LED 支持 DLMs 中更稳健的自我纠正。

Abstract
Speculative decoding is widely used to speed up generation in large language models (LLMs), with a small draft model proposing tokens that one forward pass of the target model verifies. Draft models that read the target's hidden states, such as DFlash and EAGLE-3, typically inherit the target's hidden width. We show that the draft's whole residual stream can run at half or a quarter of that width while largely preserving acceptance. For DFlash, which borrows the target's vocabulary projection, the trained output adapter folds into it, giving one narrower projection with logits unchanged up to floating-point rounding. We test two drafter families, DFlash and EAGLE-3, on two targets, Qwen3-8B (NVFP4) and GPT-OSS-20B (MXFP4), in SGLang on a B200 and a DGX Spark (GB10). At batch size 1 and temperature 0, narrowing the draft to half or a quarter width speeds up end-to-end decoding by 1.06-1.12x on B200 and 1.13-1.44x on GB10. The speedup holds at larger batch sizes. From batch 32 to the largest batch each GPU fits, narrowing reaches up to 1.21x on both GPUs, and no narrow draft is slower than full width.

A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning and Out-of-Context Hallucination
上下文学习与上下文外幻觉的机制分析
Tianxiang Chen, Jingyuan Zhou, Guoyao Yang, Kaidi Yang
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models can infer and follow specific rules through in-context learning (ICL), yet may fail to remain faithful to provided evidence, giving rise to out-of-context (OOC) hallucination. Existing work has largely investigated the underlying mechanisms of ICL and OOC hallucination along separate lines. However, this separation obscures the mechanistic basis for these seemingly opposing outcomes. In this work, we study this contrast through the unified view of functional roles in dynamic context. The key observation is that role information can be internally represented without reliably constraining output. We derive a first-order decomposition to characterize the role effect, showing that its substantial influence depends on two necessary conditions, namely sufficient contribution magnitude and coherent signed aggregation. Causal analysis further shows that role span contributions affect key token choices involving response structure, content selection, and factual values. We further show that role-consistent choices depend on sufficient role span support at these key decisions, while failing choices can be reversed when this support overcomes the deficit. These findings support a common mechanistic view of ICL and OOC hallucination: each functional role defines the pattern of output decisions over which role span contributions must remain effective, and differences in this organization account for the seemingly opposing outcomes.

大语言模型能够通过上下文学习（ICL）推断并遵循特定规则，然而可能无法忠实于所提供的证据，从而产生上下文外（OOC）幻觉。现有工作大多沿相互独立的路线研究了 ICL 与 OOC 幻觉的底层机制。然而，这种分离掩盖了这些看似相反结果背后的机制基础。在本工作中，我们通过动态上下文中功能角色的统一视角来研究这一对比。关键观察是，角色信息可以在内部得到表示，却不一定能可靠地约束输出。我们推导了一种一阶分解来刻画角色效应，表明其实质性影响取决于两个必要条件，即足够的贡献幅度和一致的带符号聚合。因果分析进一步表明，角色跨度贡献会影响涉及响应结构、内容选择和事实值的关键 token 选择。我们进一步表明，角色一致的选择取决于在这些关键决策处有足够的角色跨度支持，而当这种支持克服不足时，失败的选择可以被逆转。这些发现支持一种关于 ICL 与 OOC 幻觉的共同机制观点：每个功能角色都定义了输出决策的模式，而角色跨度贡献必须在这些决策上保持有效，这种组织方式的差异解释了这些看似相反的结果。

Andrei Kostin, José Ángel Diaz-Garcia, Karel Gutiérrez-Batista
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The growth of deceptive online opinions poses a critical risk of misinformation and fraud. This paper proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to automatically distinguish spam reviews. The architecture integrates RoBERTa with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) classification, FAISS semantic vector retrieval, and a Large Language Model (LLM) for final reasoning. The system was evaluated across balanced and severely imbalanced real-world scenarios. Results demonstrate that five epochs of fine-tuning enable robust domain transfer, achieving an F1-score of 0.90 in cross-domain evaluation, outperforming baselines (OpenAI Detector,F1 = 0.82) and demonstrating competitive performance against specialized in-domain SOTA models (fakeRoBERTa,F1 = 0.97). The proposed architecture provides evidence-backed explainability and statistically significant precision gains while maintaining comparable overall detection performance.

cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model

Abstract
Laws are increasingly turned into programs that decide cases, such as whether a firm was a small or medium enterprise (SME) on a given date, and large language models (LLMs) now write them. The programs are usually graded against answers written by someone who read the same law, so a program can score well by sharing the grader's reading rather than by getting the law right. LexTemporis grades them instead against records of what actually happened: 10,901 firm-years of SME status disclosed by Korean listed companies, with every version of the governing rules. An appendix adds comparison cases from US income tax and German hospital minimum volumes. The date changes outcomes mainly through provisions outside the main statutory text: one transitional provision raises agreement with the disclosures from 83-86% to 89-90%. The disclosures also test the author's reading of a contested provision, favouring it in 130 of 189 firm-years where readings diverge. Four LLMs wrote the rules, given different selections of the law. A pre-registered comparison finds no condition better across all four models. In exploratory analyses, supplying the right provisions looks better graded against the author's reading than against the records: the advantage shrinks for three models (for one, to between a quarter and three-fifths of its size), and per firm-year it is several times larger where the author's reading is wrong, partly by construction, since there reproducing that reading more faithfully must lose. Grading legal programs against the grader's own reading can overstate how well they work.

MIRAGE: A Framework for Multi-hop Reasoning under Dynamic Knowledge Injection
MIRAGE：动态知识注入下的多跳推理框架
Heyang Xu, HanWen Hao, Haifeng Wang, Haoyi Zhou, Jianxin Li
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Multi-hop Question Answering (MQA) requires large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and synthesize multiple pieces of evidence into a coherent reasoning path, which is essential for complex tasks. However, prior work on knowledge updating for MQA has largely focused on simple fact edits, overlooking a more challenging and realistic setting---\emph{Knowledge Injection}---in which the model must simultaneously accommodate both conflicting updates and entirely novel information. Under this setting, a hop-level answer is often wrong simply because the model trusts the wrong knowledge source: it clings to outdated parametric memory when the injected knowledge conflicts with it (K2), and it cannot answer when the required fact is entirely new (K3). To investigate this, we introduce NEXUS, the first benchmark tailored for multi-hop reasoning under Knowledge Injection, which explicitly covers both conflicting (K2) and incremental (K3) knowledge. We further propose MIRAGE, an efficient, training-free framework whose core component, the Correlation-aware Dual-path Reasoner (CDR), resolves such per-hop source-trust errors via P(True)-based confidence routing, complemented by a lightweight template-guided corrector for residual structural deviations. Extensive experiments across four LLM families and two benchmarks demonstrate that MIRAGE consistently improves both final-answer accuracy and hop-level reasoning accuracy, establishing a new state of the art in this challenging setting.

多跳问答（MQA）要求大语言模型（LLM）检索并将多条证据综合为一条连贯的推理路径，这对于复杂任务至关重要。然而，先前关于 MQA 知识更新的工作大多集中于简单的事实编辑，忽视了更具挑战性且更现实的设定——\emph{知识注入}——在该设定下，模型必须同时适应相互冲突的更新和全新的信息。在该设定下，某一跳级答案常常出错，仅仅是因为模型信任了错误的知识来源：当注入知识与参数化记忆冲突时，它固守过时的参数化记忆（K2）；而当所需事实完全新时，它无法作答（K3）。为研究这一问题，我们提出 NEXUS，这是首个专为知识注入下的多跳推理量身定制的基准，明确覆盖冲突性（K2）与增量性（K3）知识。我们进一步提出 MIRAGE，一个高效、无需训练的框架，其核心组件——相关性感知双路径推理器（CDR）——通过基于 P(True) 的置信度路由来解决此类逐跳来源信任错误，并辅以一个轻量级模板引导校正器来处理残余的结构偏差。在四个 LLM 系列和两个基准上的大量实验表明，MIRAGE 持续提升最终答案准确率和跳级推理准确率，在这一具有挑战性的设定中确立了新的最先进水平。

cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models are increasingly used to create stories for children. Since bedtime stories can shape children's perceptions of social roles, this raises concerns about whether LLMs adapt narrative portrayals according to the intended recipient's gender. We conducted a large-scale study to examine gender stereotyping in LLM-generated bedtime stories. Using matched daughter/son prompts and a five-generation design, we analyze 62,873 retained stories from 16 LLMs across 35 country settings and 12 narrator roles. We introduce a multi-level evaluation framework combining context-adjusted lexical rate contrasts, relative stereotype alignment, narrator-recipient interaction analysis, human evaluation, and representation-level interventions to examine both the consistency and interpretability of these differences. Our results reveal systematic differences in narrative framing: son-directed stories emphasize higher agency and lower communion compared to daughter-directed stories. While narrator gender expresses limited moderation on these patterns, high sociability exhibits a more pronounced interaction. Human evaluations demonstrate consistent agreement, although correspondence with lexical measures varies across narrative dimensions. Additionally, hidden-state analyses reveal decodable recipient-gender information. These findings demonstrate persistent yet context-dependent representational disparities in LLM-generated children's stories and motivate narrative-specific bias evaluation beyond short-form benchmarks.

Abstract
Judgements of sexism are subjective and may vary across communities, yet sexism detection datasets usually reduce annotator judgements to a single majority label, obscuring disagreement and how models behave on contested cases. We introduce MuDAS, a dataset of YouTube comments in Saudi, Egyptian and Moroccan Arabic, each labelled by three native speakers of its dialect, with the individual annotations preserved. We use it to evaluate Arabic encoders fine-tuned with hard-label, soft-label and perspectivist objectives, GPT-5.6 Terra, and four Arabic-centric large language models. Despite relatively close Macro-F1 scores, GPT-5.6 Terra and the fine-tuned encoders exhibit contrasting error patterns: GPT-5.6 Terra, even with the annotators' definition of sexism, over-classifies gender-related content such as religious advice on modesty, whereas the encoders miss implicit and prescriptive sexism. The Arabic-centric models also over-predict sexism and remain below the encoders. Disagreement-aware learning preserves Macro-F1, but soft labels improve alignment with annotators on contested comments at the expense of unanimous ones, and neither paradigm reliably identifies contested comments. Lower performance on Egyptian Arabic, clearest for the large language models, is not fully explained by the examined measures of test-set composition and dialectness. Majority-label scores can therefore hide contrasting error patterns that matter for content moderation.

MECI: Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction for Multimodal Entity Linking
MECI：面向多模态实体链接的多元素协同交互
Jie Peng, Yongxue Shan, Yongfu Zha, Xiaodong Wang
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Multimodal Entity Linking (MEL) aims to disambiguate mentions in multimodal contexts by grounding them to specific entities in a knowledge base. A pivotal challenge in MEL is capturing multi-level correspondences: the semantic consistency between mention-entity pairs and the complementary correlations across modalities. However, existing methods often suffer from element dominance due to their reliance on coupled interactions or coarse global aggregations. In response, we propose the Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction (MECI) framework. First, to capture multi-element mention-entity correspondences, we develop a Multi-view Experts Network that leverages a "divide-and-conquer" strategy for decoupled feature learning to mitigate element dominance, supported by a KL-guided routing mechanism that governs expert specialization and collaboration. Furthermore, to model cross-modal complementary correlations, we propose a Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Module, where a dynamic modality-aware weighting network refines interactions across hierarchical semantic levels, thereby integrating multi-granular evidence to counteract element dominance. Finally, we incorporate a generative semantic refinement stage that utilizes large language models for zero-shot re-ranking. Extensive experiments on WikiDiverse, RichpediaMEL, and WikiMEL show that MECI consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, improving Hits@1 by 1.95%, 7.30%, and 2.31%, respectively.

多模态实体链接（MEL）旨在通过将多模态上下文中的提及链接到知识库中的特定实体，从而对提及进行消歧。MEL中的一个关键挑战是捕获多级对应关系：提及-实体对之间的语义一致性以及跨模态的互补相关性。然而，现有方法由于依赖耦合交互或粗粒度全局聚合，往往受到元素主导的影响。为此，我们提出多元素协同交互（MECI）框架。首先，为了捕获多元素提及-实体对应关系，我们开发了一个多视图专家网络，该网络利用“分而治之”策略进行解耦特征学习以缓解元素主导，并由一个KL引导的路由机制支持，该机制控制专家专门化与协作。此外，为了建模跨模态互补相关性，我们提出了一个分层多模态交互模块，其中动态模态感知加权网络在分层语义层级上细化交互，从而整合多粒度证据以抵消元素主导。最后，我们引入一个生成式语义细化阶段，该阶段利用大语言模型进行零样本重排序。在WikiDiverse、RichpediaMEL和WikiMEL上的大量实验表明，MECI始终优于最先进的基线，分别将Hits@1提高了1.95%、7.30%和2.31%。

large language model

Abstract
This research investigates whether a large language model or an autonomous AI Agent performs better at translating from English to Arabic, which is considered a low-resource language. The authors introduce WikiEn-Ar190, a new dataset of 190 carefully selected Wikipedia articles from 18 different areas, which were created and verified by two native Arabic speakers to ensure that they accurately reflect both meaning and style. Using this dataset, the study evaluates the translation quality of GPT-5-mini both as an independent neural translator and when used within a more complex process that includes self-assessment and improvement. As a standalone model, GPT-5-mini produced very fluent translations , achieving a COMET score of 0.8649 and receiving high human scores for adequacy, fluency, and style (averaging 4.53 out of 5). When used in a system that combined translation with self-assessment, it improved lexical accuracy by 28.76% (BLEU score of 22.83) while maintaining a similar level of semantic quality. These findings show that methods involving autonomous reasoning can improve translation consistency for language pairs with limited resources. Beyond the results, the approach offers a framework for evaluating and improving translations, potentially using them as assisting tools to expand the representation of low resource languages, such as Arabic, on the web.

Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers
思维链隐藏状态揭示直接答案的任务求解方向
Houman Mehrafarin, Ioannis Konstas
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the performance of Large Language Models by eliciting intermediate reasoning steps. However, CoT is far from perfect: on some tasks, models perform worse than with direct-answer prompting, and on others they generate a few hundred tokens to reach the correct answer. We start by labelling each CoT hidden state as recovering if patching it into the direct prompt yields the correct answer, and failed otherwise. A linear probe shows that the model encodes these two classes differently. We then show that the representation space of the direct prompt holds a direction for each question that leads the model, in a short generation, to the correct answer more often than CoT does. Specifically, we rotate the direct prompt's last hidden state once, before generation, towards a direction built for each question from its own recovering and failed states. Across 25 tasks, these directions raise the direct prompt's mean accuracy from $46\%$ to $85\%$ on LLaMA 3.1 8B (CoT: $69\%$) and from $52\%$ to $86\%$ on Qwen 2.5 7B (CoT: $77\%$), with a tenth of CoT's tokens. CoT is thus not the shortest route to this accuracy, and these directions can be used in future work to train models to align their states with them.

思维链（CoT）提示通过引发中间推理步骤来提升大语言模型的性能。然而，CoT 远非完美：在某些任务上，模型的表现不如直接答案提示；而在另一些任务上，模型要生成数百个 token 才能得到正确答案。我们首先将每个 CoT 隐藏状态标注为“恢复型”（recovering）：如果将其修补（patch）进直接提示后能得到正确答案，则标注为恢复型，否则标注为“失败型”（failed）。线性探针表明，模型对这两类状态的编码方式不同。我们随后表明，直接提示的表示空间中存在一个针对每个问题的方向，在短生成中引导模型得到正确答案的频率高于 CoT。具体而言，在生成之前，我们将直接提示的最后一个隐藏状态一次性旋转，使其朝向一个针对每个问题、由该问题自身的恢复型状态和失败型状态构建的方向。在 25 个任务上，这些方向将直接提示的平均准确率在 LLaMA 3.1 8B 上从 $46\%$ 提升到 $85\%$（CoT：$69\%$），在 Qwen 2.5 7B 上从 $52\%$ 提升到 $86\%$（CoT：$77\%$），而仅使用 CoT 十分之一的 token。因此，CoT 并非通往这一准确率的最短路径，而这些方向可在未来工作中用于训练模型，使其状态与这些方向对齐。

Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
Clover-35B-A3B-Preview 技术报告
DiffuSpace Technical Team
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed of 680 tokens/s using one NVIDIA GB300 GPU at BF16 precision and batch size one. We organize the evaluation around model quality, drafting and verification costs, and deployment under constrained memory. We also describe a decision-model variant that generates answers to related questions in one denoising pass. On an internal set of 500 groups, joint prediction raises question accuracy from 90.37% to 93.88% and all-correct group accuracy from 65.4% to 77.0%.

我们介绍 Clover-35B-A3B-Preview（Clover），一种混合专家扩散语言模型，具有 350 亿总参数和 30 亿激活参数，支持思考模式生成。Clover 将 Gated Delta Networks 适配于块扩散，方法是将先前生成上下文的循环记忆与当前块内部的双向 softmax 注意力相结合。历史记忆读出与当前块 token 在共享 softmax 中竞争，并具有可学习的块大小校准以及一个单独的、零初始化的右上下文卷积分支。Clover 在七项被评估的智能体指标上领先，包括 SWE-bench Verified 上的 73.6 和 Terminal-Bench 2.1 上的 51.7。在内部智能体工作负载上，使用一块 NVIDIA GB300 GPU、BF16 精度和批大小为 1 时，其报告生成速度达到 680 tokens/s。我们围绕模型质量、起草与验证成本以及受限内存下的部署来组织评估。我们还描述了一种决策模型变体，它在一次去噪过程中生成对相关问题的答案。在一个包含 500 个组的内部集合上，联合预测将问题准确率从 90.37% 提高到 93.88%，并将全正确组准确率从 65.4% 提高到 77.0%。

cs.CL / 30 / 2611.24654
CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
CurvDelta：面向精准学习与遗忘的低曲率增量建模
Zeguan Xiao, Zhuocheng Liang, Yun Chen, Yong Wang, Guanhua Chen, Pinyan Lu
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. We introduce CurvDelta, a scalable framework that incorporates the preservation constraint into the parameterization of the model update. By analyzing the local geometry of the preservation constraint around the pre-adaptation model, CurvDelta constructs a low-curvature space in which parameter updates leave the preservation loss nearly invariant. We make its construction practical for LLMs through Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (K-FAC) and a factorized projection. We also introduce CurvLoRA, a low-rank variant within the same preservation geometry, designed for more efficient adaptation. Both methods apply to preservation-constrained adaptation tasks such as capability learning and selective unlearning. We evaluate our methods on mathematical reasoning, code generation, and knowledge unlearning. For mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approaches achieve competitive downstream performance while better preserving general capabilities, offering a favorable acquisition--retention trade-off relative to the baselines. For knowledge unlearning, our main results on TOFU and MUSE show a better balance between targeted forgetting and knowledge retention than the baselines, with retention performance close to the from-scratch retraining reference.

适配大语言模型（LLM）的一个核心挑战是能力保持：一次适配可以在达成其目标的同时损害通用能力。我们提出 CurvDelta，一个可扩展的框架，它将保持约束纳入模型更新的参数化之中。通过分析保持约束在适配前模型周围的局部几何，CurvDelta 构造一个低曲率空间，在该空间中参数更新使保持损失几乎不变。我们通过 Kronecker 因子化近似曲率（K-FAC）和因子化投影，使其构造对 LLM 而言切实可行。我们还提出 CurvLoRA，这是同一保持几何下的低秩变体，旨在实现更高效的适配。这两种方法都适用于受保持约束的适配任务，例如能力学习和选择性遗忘。我们在数学推理、代码生成和知识遗忘上评估我们的方法。对于数学推理和代码生成，我们的方法在取得有竞争力的下游性能的同时更好地保持通用能力，相对于基线提供了有利的获取—保持权衡。对于知识遗忘，我们在 TOFU 和 MUSE 上的主要结果表明，与基线相比，在定向遗忘和知识保持之间取得了更好的平衡，其保持性能接近从头重训练的参考。

A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
一个用于测量和预测人类行为的基础模型
Haoran Ye, Tianrui Huo, Hangzhen Li, Xin Zhang, Guojie Song
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.HC
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological constructs. In our evaluations, Chiron's psychological measurements agree more closely with human self-reports and exhibit fewer biases that undermine psychometric validity. It predicts individual behaviour more accurately than frontier LLMs (up to 28.4% relative improvement). In simulations of social science experiments, it more accurately captures the direction and magnitude of human experimental effects (82.2--94.3% lower effect-size estimation error). Together, these results establish Chiron as a unified computational instrument for measuring and predicting human behaviour.

Ground, Iterate, Trace: Decomposing AI Research Ideation
扎根、迭代、追踪：分解 AI 研究构思
Samson Yu, Qiran Zou, Jing Yu Lim, Rushi Shah, Anirudh Goyal, Dianbo Liu
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models have been widely used to generate plausible research ideas, yet it remains unclear what makes automated ideation effective and how generated novel proposals arise from prior scientific work. We introduce the Creative AI Researcher (CAR), an agentic framework combining literature grounding, iterative development and explicit conceptual operators. CAR constructs a semantic knowledge graph from retrieved literature and equips an ideation agent with graph-retrieval tools and four operators: bisociation, analogy, exploration and elaboration. Each operator call is checked against structural acceptance conditions and recorded, producing a trace of intermediate transformations and declared literature sources. We evaluate CAR with two language-model backbones across 40 LiveIdeaBench research topics and two execution benchmarks. CAR achieves significantly higher methodological novelty (MN) than single-shot prompting and The AI Scientist. Its methodological novelty does not differ significantly from the Research Ideation Agent, while its feasibility scores are higher on both backbones. With a shared experiment executor, CAR achieves the highest pairwise win rate among the evaluated AI methods on FML-bench-Lite and BioXArena. In a ten-condition ablation study, MN point estimates favor CAR over one-step proposal on both backbones, but no MN contrast survives correction for multiple comparisons. The results do not establish a consistent quality benefit from explicit operators beyond free-form iteration. CAR makes the sequence of operations and declared literature sources inspectable, separating judged idea quality from procedural traceability.

Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures

cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Jailbreak attempts and harmful prompts remain a challenge for the safe deployment of large language models. We study whether contrastively learned representations can support safety detection without training an additional downstream classifier. We propose Jailbreak Detection with Prototype Inference (JDPI), which uses binary safety labels to construct harmful and benign prototypes and makes predictions from relative prototype distances. JDPI uses only binary safety labels for encoder adaptation, prototype construction, and validation. In our setup, it uses fewer labeled examples than the classifier baseline (Method A) by avoiding the separate split used to train the downstream classifier. Across four benchmarks covering different input formats, contrastive fine-tuning improves JDPI's detection accuracy by 9.1-18.0 percentage points. Using the same encoder, JDPI achieves slightly higher ROC-AUC on one benchmark and stays within 0.017 of the baseline across all four. With dataset-specific adaptation, JDPI exceeds the released Llama Guard 3-8B baseline by 0.173-0.310 in ROC-AUC across the four benchmarks. In multi-turn replay on TomGibbs, JDPI uses accumulated user history as the conversation unfolds, achieving higher conversation-level accuracy than when it uses the current turn alone. Across 12 directed transfers, JDPI outperforms the classifier by an average of 1.59 percentage points in accuracy, demonstrating stronger cross-dataset robustness.

Lossless Reversible Watermarking for AIGC with Applications in Authentication

cs.CR · cs.CV

扩散模型相关
Abstract
AIGC watermarking is commonly used for tracing, but it can also support applications such as authentication and tampering detection. We study lossless reversible watermarking, which enables exact recovery of the original watermarked image after permissible distortions. By exploiting the relatively low entropy of the information required for image generation, together with robust latent-space watermarking, we design a framework that preserves sufficient information for lossless recovery. We then apply the framework to AIGC authentication, which generally faces two key challenges. First, the authentication mechanism must resist adaptive adversaries. Second, the content relevant to authentication, such as visual designs or expressed messages, may depend on application requirements that are not known at generation time. To solve these difficulties, we incorporate cryptographic message authentication to provide unforgeability against adaptive attacks. Lossless recovery provides the original image as reference evidence, after which a suitable analyzer can be selected to make the authentication decision. Experiments on Stable Diffusion demonstrate exact recovery under a wide range of distortions.

Abstract
Phishing remains a major source of credential theft and fraudulent payments, and email security systems must classify large message volumes reliably, quickly, and at manageable cost. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer flexible text understanding, but their token-based generation increases response time and API cost, and the reliability of their confidence values requires measurement. Jev 1.13, a typed decision model from TypeSafe AI, instead returns a structured outcome with a confidence value. This paper compares Jev 1.13 with Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, and Meta Llama 4 Maverick on a labelled dataset of 1500 emails, covering classification performance, decision latency, token consumption, API cost, and probability calibration. Jev achieves the highest accuracy (79.67%), precision (71.43%), recall (97.97%), and F1 score (82.62%). It also records the shortest batch time (173.88 seconds), the lowest token count (597,895), the lowest cost (USD 0.015103 per 1000 decisions), and the lowest Brier score (0.1698) and ECE (0.1594). These results suggest that Jev is a promising option for fast, structured, high-volume triage. LLMs retain the advantage of generating explanations, which we do not evaluate, and all four systems require further validation before standalone deployment.

Plug-and-Play Multi-Licensee Robust Watermarking for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures enable high-capacity large language models (LLMs) with high sparse computation, making them attractive for deployment on private hardware. However, distributing model weights exposes valuable intellectual property (IP) to leakage and unauthorized redistribution, creating an urgent need to both verify model ownership and trace leaked copies to individual licensees. Existing model-watermarking techniques are ill-suited for meeting this need because they are fragile under MoE's dynamic routing or require costly retraining to embed a distinct watermark for each licensee, thus making scalable distribution difficult. To address these challenges, we present PPMoE, the first plug-and-play multi-licensee watermarking framework for MoE LLMs. Rather than training a separate model per user, PPMoE trains a compact set of mergeable incremental weight modules that steer the MoE router toward distinct, mutually compatible routing patterns. During model distribution, the model owner selectively merges unique combinations of these pre-trained, mutually compatible modules into the base model on the fly, embedding a licensee-specific watermark without additional training. PPMoE supports reliable multi-licensee attribution under both white- and black-box threat models. In the white-box setting, attribution is done by inspecting triggered routing decisions or the merged weight modules responsible for these decisions, whereas in the black-box setting, attribution relies on analyzing output token likelihood ratios. Extensive experiments across five state-of-the-art MoE models, seven benchmark datasets, and varying number of licensees show that PPMoE achieves very high attribution accuracy while preserving base model utility and maintaining strong robustness to various adaptive watermark-removal attacks.

large language model

Abstract
Network discovery, the identification of live hosts and their exposed services, is the first phase of every penetration test, and it is increasingly automated by harnesses driven by large language models (LLMs). To mitigate hallucinated or unsafe commands, recent work proposes inserting fast, non-generative decision models to validate actions prior to execution. This paper quantifies whether such validation improves discovery across three network scales (n = 10, 100, and 1,000) in a simulation calibrated on a 30-node containerized testbed. Our findings show that chunked batch dispatch recovers 92% to 100% of open ports in large-scale networks, whereas single-host dispatch collapses to under 6% due to context saturation and scan latency. Furthermore, at the measured proposal quality of the local model, decision gating increases its port recall from 75.5% to 89.0% on small networks and intercepts costly decoy tarpits, but it imposes additional latency on frontier models during early host discovery.

PIVOT: Distribution-Preserving Multi-BitWatermarking with Minimax-Optimal Scoring
PIVOT：具有极小极大最优评分的分布保持多比特水印
Wen Zhang, Kaiyi Pang, Minhao Bai, Shuyu Gan, Liping Zhu
cs.CR · stat.AP
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
As LLM-generated content becomes increasingly widespread, reliable attribution calls for multi-bit watermarks that embed recoverable messages without distorting the output distribution. We introduce PIVOT, a multi-bit watermark with model-free verification based on mirrored rank-interval sampling. At each generation step, PIVOT uses a keyed pseudorandom scalar and a secret permutation of the vocabulary. The message bit determines whether next-token probability intervals are arranged in forward or reverse secret-rank order. Sampling from these mirrored layouts preserves every token probability exactly while inducing an opposite-signed dependence between the scalar and the sampled token's secret rank. This dependence yields a pivotal rank statistic whose null distribution is invariant to the unknown next-token law, enabling model-free calibration and decoding. We formulate joint watermark detection and message recovery as a multiple-hypothesis testing problem, derive a moment-robust minimax-optimal detection score over a relaxed moment class, and establish finite-sample recovery guarantees. Extensive experiments on two representative large language models validate the effectiveness of PIVOT, demonstrating reliable watermark detection and message recovery while preserving the generator's output distribution.

Evaluating LIM Trading Agents: A Critical Review of Backtesting Validity and Reporting Practices
评估 LIM 交易智能体：对回测有效性与报告实践的批判性综述
Long Xu, Fuyi Wang, Xiaolu Hu, Chao Chen
cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in investment research, and many studies report promising historical returns. However, such results are only credible if researchers can demonstrate that the model used only information available at the time, account for how strategies and configurations were selected, and explain how reported returns were generated. We identify six common threats to validity in LLM investment evaluations and apply them to 18 published studies. Across 108 assessments, we find substantial gaps in reporting. No paper fully addresses information timing, model-memory exposure, universe selection, trading costs, or configuration-selection bias. Only four studies provide minimum evidence that results hold across multiple market periods. Our analysis reveals that commonly used safeguards often address different problems than researchers assume. For example, using dated inputs does not guarantee that a pretrained model lacked knowledge of future events, and repeated experimental runs do not correct for strategy-selection bias. We therefore propose an evaluation protocol for future LLM investment research. Rather than judging whether LLMs can generate profits, our study examines whether existing evidence is sufficient to support such claims. We conclude that current reporting practices are generally insufficient for that purpose.

Guarding the Kingdom of Skill-Based Agents in the AI Dynasty of Computation: Control-Flow Integrity for Agent Skills

Bonan Ruan, Yuhao Sun, Jiahao Liu, Qixiao Lin, Jian Mao, Zhenkai Liang
cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Control-flow integrity (CFI) confines a program to a control-flow graph fixed ahead of time. Procedural agent skills move this control flow into prompt text, and a large language model (LLM) agent decides at runtime whether each step runs in its reasoning, a tool call, or a script. The procedure's control skeleton survives, but its enforceability depends on where each step runs. Many violations, such as overwriting a file before validation, use only operations the skill requires, so permission allowlists admit them. A deviating or prompt-injected model can also evade a monitor by regime migration, for example by claiming that a check passed. We present SkillCFI, which carries CFI over to skill-based agents. Its compiler confines LLM interpretation to compile time and derives the agent's instructions and an executable contract from one skill. By a formal enforceability criterion, it enforces obligations whose evidence crosses the tool boundary and rejects a skill whose mandatory obligation leaves nothing to check. A deterministic runtime enforcer admits a tool request only on trusted evidence and refuses unmediated channels such as inline scripts, so admitted traces follow the contract whatever the model proposes. On eight self-written skills, no compiled contract permits more than its source under 24 source mutations. In 770 agent sessions, SkillCFI blocks before dispatch all 240 such violations, which an allowlist admits, and normal tasks complete nearly as often as without it. Listing the next legal steps in a refusal raises recovery from 21% to 65%. Checking takes about 2% of task time, and a compact command form cuts session slowdown from 1.32 times to 1.08 times. None of 53 public skills is accepted as written. The compiler's diagnostics point to interfaces rather than workflows and guided seven into enforceable contracts.

Erased but Recoverable: On the Fragility of Concept Erasure Under Fine-Tuning
已被擦除但仍可恢复：论微调下概念擦除的脆弱性
Jun Li, Lizhi Xiong, Ziqiang Li, Yu Liu, Zenglin Shi
cs.CR
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Existing concept erasure methods for text-to-image diffusion models primarily focus on suppressing target concepts while preserving non-target generation quality. However, in practical applications, open-source diffusion models are often further adapted through DreamBooth, LoRA, or Custom Diffusion. Such adaptations can reshape internal representations, thereby weakening or even reversing the erasure effects achieved by existing methods. We identify erasure persistence as a key yet underexplored dimension of concept erasure and analyze how downstream fine-tuning reshapes internal representations. Our analysis reveals that fine-tuning of the original model does not uniformly modify the model, but preserves certain high-contribution structures, particularly attention heads with stable output subspaces and response magnitudes. We also observe that, after downstream fine-tuning of concept-erased models, these heads' output representations more readily realign with their pretrained counterparts. Motivated by this observation, we propose Stable-Head-Aware Concept Erasure (SHACE), which improves erasure persistence by preserving stable attention structures during concept erasure. SHACE identifies stability-critical attention heads through Attention-Head Stability Profiling and keeps their corresponding parameter blocks unchanged during erasure via Stable-Head Gradient Preservation. Extensive experiments show that SHACE improves resistance to concept recovery across diverse fine-tuning settings while maintaining strong suppression and non-target generation quality.

现有的文本到图像扩散模型概念擦除方法主要关注在抑制目标概念的同时保持非目标生成质量。然而，在实际应用中，开源扩散模型常常通过 DreamBooth、LoRA 或 Custom Diffusion 进行进一步适配。此类适配能够重塑内部表征，从而削弱甚至逆转现有方法所取得的擦除效果。我们将擦除持久性确定为一个关键但尚未被充分探索的概念擦除维度，并分析下游微调如何重塑内部表征。我们的分析揭示，对原始模型的微调并非均匀地修改模型，而是保留某些高贡献结构，特别是具有稳定输出子空间和响应幅度的注意力头。我们还观察到，在对概念已擦除的模型进行下游微调之后，这些头的输出表征更容易与其预训练对应物重新对齐。受这一观察启发，我们提出稳定头感知的概念擦除（Stable-Head-Aware Concept Erasure，SHACE），它通过在概念擦除过程中保留稳定的注意力结构来提升擦除持久性。SHACE 通过注意力头稳定性剖析（Attention-Head Stability Profiling）识别对稳定性至关重要的注意力头，并通过稳定头梯度保持（Stable-Head Gradient Preservation）在擦除过程中使其对应的参数块保持不变。大量实验表明，SHACE 在多种微调设置下提升了对概念恢复的抵抗能力，同时保持了强力的抑制效果和非目标生成质量。

PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
PIPETTE：面向鲁棒 LLM 智能体的提示注入紫队测试
Lipeng He, Yihan Wang, Jiawen Zhang, N. Asokan
cs.CR · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents routinely interact with untrusted external data, exposing them to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks that hijack agents into executing attacker-chosen tasks. To uncover these vulnerabilities at scale, automated red-teaming methods often leverage reinforcement learning (RL) to generate attacks that achieve high attack success rates (ASR). Model developers use the attacks discovered during internal red-teaming to harden agents through adversarial training before deployment, a collaborative offensive-defensive process known in cybersecurity as purple-teaming. However, we show that achieving high ASR during red-teaming does not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training. Specifically, we find that two state-of-the-art RL-based red-teaming methods, RL-Hammer and PISmith, suffer from mode collapse, repeatedly discovering similar attack strategies whose additional successes add no additional robustness improvements to adversarial training. To address this gap, we introduce PIPETTE, a unified prompt injection purple-teaming framework that effectively converts red-teaming discoveries into defender robustness improvements. PIPETTE employs a dictionary learning-based reward that encourages broader coverage of attack strategies during red-teaming. It also integrates an on-policy adversarial training pipeline tailored to IPI defense, enabling agents to resist attacks while completing legitimate user tasks. Extensive evaluations across agentic benchmarks (AgentDojo and ASB) demonstrate that PIPETTE produces defenders that achieve near-zero attack success rates on static attacks and can withstand strong adaptive attacks, while maintaining benign task utility close to that of the undefended baseline.

LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids
智能电网中LLM引导的信息物理攻击路径识别
Amr Elshazly, Jesse Roberts, Rachad Atat, Muhammad Ismail
cs.CR · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Identifying high-impact attack paths in cyber-physical power systems is critical for improving grid resilience. Existing methods typically rely on either structural topology analysis or simulation-based cascading-failure models. Topology-based approaches capture connectivity but lack adversarial reasoning, while simulation-driven methods are primarily suited for offline analysis and are less effective for rapid evaluation of evolving attack scenarios. As a result, identifying realistic attack paths that jointly capture topology, threat semantics, and physical impact remains challenging. This paper presents a physics-grounded framework for identifying cyber-physical attack paths using large language models (LLMs), with cascading-failure-derived impact rankings used as physics-grounded references. The framework integrates system topology, LLM-guided STRIDE and MITRE ATT&CK threat modeling, and three baseline strategies for comparison: topology-driven, threat-driven, and fusion-based. Evaluation is performed using (i) critical-node overlap between LLM-inferred top-K rankings and cascading-failure-based ground truth; (ii) node-level similarity between LLM-inferred and reference paths; and (iii) path-level alignment capturing agreement in complete attack sequences. Results show that structured LLM-based threat modeling substantially improves alignment with physics-grounded references. In the cyber layer, critical-node overlap@3 increases from approximately 33% to as high as 100%, while node-level similarity reaches up to 65% and path-level alignment reaches up to 48%. In addition, the proposed framework reduces runtime by approximately 75--85% compared to the fusion-based baseline in the IEEE 14-bus system. These results suggest that LLM-guided attack path identification is a promising approach for efficient and impact-aware cyber-physical security analysis.

Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks
共价有机框架衍射数据的结构化提取

cs.CV · cond-mat.mtrl-sci · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) is the primary structural evidence for covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and many other materials. Yet decades of measured patterns exist only as images in published figures. Automatic recovery is difficult, because PXRD figures vary widely in format, from a single curve to crowded stacks with labels, insets, and neighboring plots that challenge traditional computer vision. This work presents a pipeline in which a vision large language model (LLM) interprets the layout of each figure, locating the diffraction plot and its curves and sketching a coarse trace of each, while classical computer vision (CV) refines every trace to pixel-level accuracy. Applied to 3,954 COF articles, the pipeline produces 11,445 calibrated diffraction curves, released in the open database COF-PEAK. Compared with a hand digitization of 60 panels, extracted peak positions differ by a median of only 0.07 degrees. Whereas papers usually report only a few peak angles, which limits further analysis, the digitized curves enable tracking how peak prominence, a possible marker of crystallinity, changes with synthesis conditions. Vision LLMs and classical CV can thus turn such figures into reusable experimental data.

ReflectScene：MLLM引导的闭环扩散用于3D室内场景生成
Jiawei Shen, Jie Feng, Junpeng Zhang, Guanbin Li, Wanyi Chen, Weisheng Dong, Guangming Shi
cs.CV · cs.AI
diffusionlarge language model
扩散模型相关
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation requires layouts satisfying geometric, functional, and semantic constraints. However, existing diffusion methods rely primarily on static textual conditions, limiting their ability to assess evolving scenes and translate semantic discrepancies into executable object-level corrections. MLLM-based post-hoc refinement provides semantic feedback but remains decoupled from denoising, potentially disrupting scene coherence.We propose ReflectScene, an MLLM-guided closed-loop diffusion framework. First, we introduce Hierarchical Prior-Grounded Scene Understanding that aligns structured layouts with multi-view visual evidence, to interpret object-specific context and scene global semantics via a frozen multi-modal large language model (MLLM). Second, we propose MLLM-Guided Semantic Reward Evaluation to distill MLLM's diagnoses and assessments on possible candidate corrections into a lightweight Reward Predictor, enabling correction decision making with reduced computation burden. Finally, Decision-Conditioned Trajectory-Consistent Diffusion is proposed to integrate selected corrections through transient conditioning and persistent clean-estimate projection, correcting object layout in the generated scene while preserving non-target arrangements throughout denoising.Experiments on 3D-FRONT demonstrate improved functional consistency and semantic alignment while maintaining competitive generation quality and diversity.

NullTok: empirical-null token selection for training-free long video understanding
